svg.title: Respiration, exercise & metabolism
svg.desc: Aerobic respiration: Glucose + oxygen → CO₂ + water. Mostly in mitochondria; complete oxidation. Exothermic, continuous in living cells; energy for movement, keeping warm and building molecules. Respiration is not breathing; energy is transferred, not created. Anaerobic & fermentation: Muscles: glucose → lactic acid. Yeast/plants: glucose → ethanol + CO₂. No oxygen required. Incomplete breakdown transfers much less energy per glucose than aerobic respiration. Yeast fermentation: CO₂ raises bread dough; ethanol makes alcoholic drinks. During exercise: Heart rate and breathing rate/volume increase, delivering more oxygenated blood to muscles. If oxygen supply cannot meet demand, anaerobic respiration increases → lactic acid builds up. Prolonged vigorous activity → fatigue and less efficient contraction. Recovery & investigation: Oxygen debt: extra oxygen needed after exercise to deal with accumulated lactic acid. Blood carries it to liver → glucose. Compare resting/post-exercise pulse; standardise time/pace, allow recovery, repeat and use safe activities. 15-second pulse count × 4 = beats/min. Building molecules: Metabolism = all reactions in cells/body. Enzymes control reactions; respiration supplies energy. Glucose → starch (plants), glycogen (animals), cellulose (plant walls). 1 glycerol + 3 fatty acids → lipid. Protein & waste: Plants: glucose + nitrate-derived nitrogen → amino acids → proteins. Excess proteins/amino acids are broken down, producing urea for excretion. Digestion supplies small molecules; cells rebuild their own materials. Respiration is one part of metabolism.
